title: "AFL: Coverage-guided Greybox Fuzzing"
description: |
  Implement the core AFL (American Fuzzy Lop) fuzzing algorithm with full paper-faithful
  mechanisms including: 64KB shared memory bitmap with hit count bucketing (1,2,3,4-7,8-15,
  16-31,32-127,128+), edge coverage tracking via (prev_block XOR cur_block)>>1, fork server

  during bitflip, user+auto dictionary insertion), havoc stage (random stacked mutations 2^1-2^7
  operations), splice stage (midpoint combination of two seeds followed by havoc), performance
  scoring based on exec speed/coverage/depth/stability, crash deduplication via coverage hash,
  and queue scheduling with favored seed priority (75/25 split).

=========== requirements/aflfast.yaml ===========
slug: aflfast
title: "AFLFast: Power Schedules via Markov Chain Model"
description: |
  Implement AFLFast's power schedules based on modeling fuzzing as a Markov chain.
  Each unique execution path is a state; mutations cause transitions between states.
  The key insight is that AFL's constant energy wastes effort on high-frequency paths.
  AFLFast assigns energy inversely proportional to path frequency f(i) and exponentially
  in selection count s(i). Includes: EXPLOIT schedule (p(i)=alpha, same as AFL),
  EXPLORE schedule (p(i)=alpha/beta, normalized), COE schedule (cut-off exponential:
  skip seeds with f(i)>mu, otherwise min(alpha/beta * 2^s(i), M)), FAST schedule
  (recommended: min(alpha/beta * 2^s(i) / f(i), M)), LINEAR schedule (min(alpha/beta *
  s(i)/f(i), M)), QUAD schedule (min(alpha/beta * s(i)^2/f(i), M)). Also implements
  PathFrequencyTracker (Markov state identification, transition counting, rare path
  detection), seed prioritization strategies (prioritize_small_s for FAST/COE,
  prioritize_small_f for explore/linear/quad), EnergyComputer with Gini coefficient
  analysis, and schedule comparison utilities.
depends_on:
  - afl
files_to_create:
  - fuzzsim/aflfast_schedules.py
  - fuzzsim/aflfast_search.py
  - fuzzsim/experiments/aflfast_experiment.py
files_to_modify:
  - run.sh
concepts:
  - Markov chain path model
  - path frequency tracking (f(i) = inputs exercising path i)
  - selection count tracking (s(i) = times seed i was chosen)
  - power schedule variants (FAST, COE, explore, exploit, linear, quad)
  - energy assignment formulas (exponential, linear, quadratic)
  - cut-off mechanism (skip over-fuzzed seeds)
  - upper bound M on energy (prevent explosion)
  - seed prioritization by s(i) and f(i)
  - Markov state transitions and probability estimation
  - rare path identification and bonus
  - energy distribution analysis (Gini coefficient)
expected_outputs:
  AFLFAST_PATHS_FAST: 10
  AFLFAST_PATHS_COE: 10
  AFLFAST_SPEEDUP: 1.00
  AFLFAST_MEAN_ENERGY: 198.5
=========== requirements/aflgo.yaml ===========
slug: aflgo
title: "AFLGo: Directed Greybox Fuzzing"
description: |
  Implement AFLGo's directed greybox fuzzing with distance-based seed prioritization
  and simulated annealing for exploration-to-exploitation transition. Two-level distance
  computation: (1) Function-level via BFS on reverse call graph from target functions,
  (2) Basic-block level combining CFG shortest paths with function distances via harmonic
  mean. CallGraph class with function/edge management. CFGDistance class with BFS-based
  shortest path computation. Distance normalization to [0,1] range. Seed distance via
  minimum block distance among covered edges. Simulated annealing with exponential cooling
  schedule T(t)=T0*alpha^(t/t_x*K), plus alternative cooling schedules (linear: T0*(1-t/t_x),
  logarithmic: T0/(1+log(1+t/t_x*K)), adaptive: adjusts alpha based on progress). Energy
  assignment formula: p(s,T)=base*((1-d(s))*(1-T)+0.5*T) transitioning from uniform (T=1)
  to distance-proportional (T=0). Seed skipping during exploitation phase (T<0.3, d>0.9).
  DistanceComputer class orchestrating the full pipeline. Phase detection (exploration/
  transition/exploitation).
depends_on:
  - afl
files_to_create:
  - fuzzsim/aflgo_distance.py
  - fuzzsim/aflgo_annealing.py
  - fuzzsim/experiments/aflgo_experiment.py
files_to_modify:
  - run.sh
concepts:
  - directed greybox fuzzing
  - call graph construction and BFS traversal
  - CFG shortest path computation
  - function-level distance via reverse BFS
  - basic-block level distance via harmonic mean
  - distance normalization to [0,1]
  - seed distance aggregation (minimum, harmonic mean)
  - simulated annealing (exponential cooling)
  - alternative cooling schedules (linear, logarithmic, adaptive)
  - exploration vs exploitation phases
  - temperature-based energy assignment
  - seed skipping during exploitation
  - time-to-exposure (TTE) metric

  AFLGO_DIRECTED_TTE: 939
  AFLGO_UNDIRECTED_TTE: 1103
  AFLGO_SPEEDUP: 1.17
=========== requirements/aflpp.yaml ===========
slug: aflpp
title: "AFL++: Modular Fuzzing Framework"
description: |
  Implement AFL++'s modular framework with full custom mutator API and MOpt PSO-based
  mutation scheduling. Custom Mutator API matching AFL++ afl-fuzz-mutator.c: init(),
  fuzz(buf, add_buf), fuzz_count(buf), havoc_mutation(buf, max_size),
  havoc_mutation_probability(), post_process(buf), trim(buf), describe(),
  queue_new_entry(buf, coverage). MutatorRegistry: register/unregister mutators,
  weighted random selection, dynamic weight adjustment (1.1x on success, 0.99x on
  failure, min 0.1). Built-in mutators: GrammarMutator (token templates, structured
  input generation, grammar-aware trimming), CmpLogMutator (RedQueen comparison
  operand recording and substitution for bypassing magic bytes). MOpt PSO scheduler:
  pilot phase (independent operator testing, L iterations each), core phase (PSO
  velocity update: v=w*v+c1*r1*(pbest-x)+c2*r2*(gbest-x), position update: x=x+v,
  velocity clamping [-0.3, 0.3], probability bounds [0.02, 0.50], normalization to
  valid distribution). Operator set: bit_flip, byte_flip, arith_add, arith_sub,
  interesting, random_byte, havoc_1, havoc_2. Personal/global best tracking, fitness
  history, convergence monitoring. PowerScheduleEnsemble: rotate through FAST/COE/
  EXPLORE/QUAD/LIN schedules per queue cycle.
depends_on:
  - afl

slug: fairfuzz
title: "FairFuzz: Targeted Mutation for Rare Branches"
description: |
  Implement FairFuzz's approach to improving coverage of rare branches by identifying
  under-covered edges, detecting input-to-branch influence via differential mutation,
  and applying targeted mutations that preserve rare branch hits. Rare branch
  identification: count seeds per edge, edges with count <= threshold are "rare".

    94	    in loop trip counts do not look like new coverage::
    95	
    96	        1, 2, 3, 4-7, 8-15, 16-31, 32-127, 128+
    97	    """
    98	    if count < 0:
    99	        raise ValueError("hit count must be non-negative")

   102	            return bucket
   103	    return 128

   148	# "Could this value have been produced by a cheaper stage?" predicates
   149	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   150	
   151	def could_be_bitflip(xor_val: int) -> bool:
   152	    """True if ``xor_val`` is reachable by the walking bit-flip stages.
   153	
   154	    Direct port of afl-fuzz.c's could_be_bitflip(): 1/2/4 bit patterns are
   155	    reachable at any offset, 8/16/32 bit patterns only at byte-aligned ones.
   156	    """
   157	    xor_val &= 0xFFFFFFFF
   158	    if xor_val == 0:
   159	        return True
   160	    sh = 0
   161	    while (xor_val & 1) == 0:
   162	        sh += 1
   163	        xor_val >>= 1
   164	    if xor_val in (1, 3, 15):
   165	        return True
   166	    if sh & 7:
   167	        return False
   168	    return xor_val in (0xFF, 0xFFFF, 0xFFFFFFFF)
   169	
   170	
   171	def _within_arith(a: int, b: int, bits: int) -> bool:
   172	    """True if ``a`` and ``b`` are within ARITH_MAX using wrapping arithmetic."""
   173	    mask = (1 << bits) - 1
   174	    return ((a - b) & mask) <= ARITH_MAX or ((b - a) & mask) <= ARITH_MAX
   175	
   176	
   177	def could_be_arith(old_val: int, new_val: int, blen: int) -> bool:
   178	    """True if ``old_val -> new_val`` is reachable by the arithmetic stages."""
   179	    if old_val == new_val:
   180	        return True
   181	
   182	    diffs = 0
   183	    ov = nv = 0
   184	    for i in range(blen):
   185	        a = (old_val >> (8 * i)) & 0xFF
   186	        b = (new_val >> (8 * i)) & 0xFF
   187	        if a != b:
   188	            diffs += 1
   189	            ov, nv = a, b
   190	
   191	    # A single byte differs: an 8 bit arithmetic op would have found it.
   192	    if diffs == 1 and _within_arith(ov, nv, 8):
   193	        return True
   194	
   195	    if blen == 1:
   196	        return False
   197	
   198	    # Try 16 bit arithmetics in both endiannesses.
   199	    diffs = 0
   200	    for i in range(blen // 2):
   201	        a = (old_val >> (16 * i)) & 0xFFFF
   202	        b = (new_val >> (16 * i)) & 0xFFFF
   203	        if a != b:
   204	            diffs += 1
   205	            ov, nv = a, b
   206	    if diffs == 1:
   207	        if _within_arith(ov, nv, 16):
   208	            return True
   209	        if _within_arith(swap16(ov), swap16(nv), 16):
   210	            return True
   211	
   212	    if blen == 4:
   213	        if _within_arith(old_val, new_val, 32):
   214	            return True
   215	        if _within_arith(swap32(old_val), swap32(new_val), 32):
   216	            return True
   217	    return False
   218	
   219	
   220	def could_be_interest(old_val: int, new_val: int, blen: int, check_le: bool) -> bool:
   221	    """True if ``old_val -> new_val`` is reachable by the interesting-value stages."""
   222	    if old_val == new_val:
   223	        return True
   224	
   225	    # Single-byte interesting values applied at any offset.
   226	    for i in range(blen):
   227	        for interesting in INTERESTING_8:
   228	            tval = (old_val & ~(0xFF << (8 * i))) | ((interesting & 0xFF) << (8 * i))
   229	            if new_val == tval:
   230	                return True
   231	
   232	    if blen == 2 and not check_le:
   233	        return False
   234	
   235	    for i in range(blen - 1):
   236	        for interesting in INTERESTING_16:
   237	            iv = interesting & 0xFFFF
   238	            tval = (old_val & ~(0xFFFF << (8 * i))) | (iv << (8 * i))
   239	            if new_val == tval:
   240	                return True
   241	            if blen > 2:
   242	                tval = (old_val & ~(0xFFFF << (8 * i))) | (swap16(iv) << (8 * i))
   243	                if new_val == tval:
   244	                    return True
   245	    return False

   251	
   252	class ForkServer:
   253	    """Simulated AFL fork server.
   254	
   255	    The real fork server executes the target up to ``main()`` once and then
   256	    clones the initialised process for every test case, which removes the
   257	    (expensive) linking/initialisation cost from the per-exec budget.  We model
   258	    that: ``STARTUP_COST`` is paid once at ``start()`` and every subsequent run
   259	    only pays ``FORK_COST`` plus the target's own execution time.
   260	    """
   261	
   262	    STARTUP_COST = 0.020  # 20ms one-off initialisation
   263	    FORK_COST = 0.0002    # 0.2ms per fork
   264	    EXECVE_COST = 0.010   # 10ms if we had to execve() every time
   265	
   266	    def __init__(self, program):
   267	        self.program = program
   268	        self.is_running = False
   269	        self.total_execs = 0
   270	        self.total_time = 0.0
   271	        self.startup_time = 0.0
   272	        self.timeouts = 0
   273	        self.child_pid = 0
   274	
   275	    def start(self) -> None:
   276	        """Spin up the fork server (paid once)."""
   277	        if self.is_running:
   278	            return
   279	        self.is_running = True
   280	        self.startup_time = self.STARTUP_COST
   281	        self.total_time += self.STARTUP_COST
   282	        self.child_pid = 1000
   283	
   284	    def run(self, data: bytes) -> Tuple[Set[int], bool, float]:
   285	        """Execute one test case through the fork server."""
   286	        if not self.is_running:
   287	            self.start()
   288	        self.child_pid += 1
   289	        edges, is_crash, exec_time = self.program.execute(data)
   290	        self.total_execs += 1
   291	        self.total_time += self.FORK_COST + exec_time
   292	        return set(edges), bool(is_crash), float(exec_time)
   293	
   294	    def stop(self) -> None:
   295	        self.is_running = False
   296	        self.child_pid = 0
   297	
   298	    @property
   299	    def saved_time(self) -> float:
   300	        """Time saved compared to a plain execve() based executor."""
   301	        return self.total_execs * (self.EXECVE_COST - self.FORK_COST) - self.STARTUP_COST

   306	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   307	
   308	class AFLBitmap:
   309	    """64KB coverage bitmap with hit-count bucketing and virgin-bit tracking."""
   310	
   311	    def __init__(self, map_size: int = MAP_SIZE):
   312	        self.map_size = map_size
   313	        # virgin_bits[edge] is the OR of every bucket value observed so far.
   314	        self.virgin_bits: Dict[int, int] = {}
   315	        self.global_coverage: Set[int] = set()
   316	        self.hit_counts: Dict[int, int] = {}
   317	        self.trace_bits: Dict[int, int] = {}
   318	
   319	    # -- current run ------------------------------------------------------
   320	    def reset_trace(self) -> None:
   321	        self.trace_bits = {}
   322	
   323	    def record_trace(self, edges: Dict[int, int]) -> None:
   324	        """Store the raw hit counts of the current execution."""
   325	        self.trace_bits = dict(edges)
   326	
   327	    def classified_trace(self) -> Dict[int, int]:
   328	        """Return the current trace after classify_counts()."""
   329	        return {e: classify_counts(c) for e, c in self.trace_bits.items()}
   330	
   331	    # -- global bitmap ----------------------------------------------------
   332	    def has_new_bits(self, edges: Dict[int, int]) -> int:
   333	        """AFL's has_new_bits(): 2 = new edge, 1 = new hit-count bucket, 0 = nothing."""
   334	        result = 0
   335	        for edge, count in edges.items():
   336	            if count <= 0:
   337	                continue
   338	            bucket = classify_counts(count)
   339	            seen = self.virgin_bits.get(edge, 0)
   340	            if seen == 0:
   341	                return 2
   342	            if seen & bucket == 0:
   343	                result = max(result, 1)
   344	        return result
   345	
   346	    def update(self, edges: Dict[int, int]) -> Set[int]:
   347	        """Fold an execution into the global bitmap, returning new edges."""
   348	        new_edges = set()
   349	        for edge, count in edges.items():
   350	            if count <= 0:
   351	                continue
   352	            if edge not in self.virgin_bits:
   353	                new_edges.add(edge)
   354	                self.virgin_bits[edge] = 0
   355	            self.virgin_bits[edge] |= classify_counts(count)
   356	            self.global_coverage.add(edge)
   357	            self.hit_counts[edge] = self.hit_counts.get(edge, 0) + count
   358	        return new_edges
   359	
   360	    def count_bytes(self) -> int:
   361	        """Number of non-zero bytes in the bitmap (AFL's count_bytes)."""
   362	        return len(self.global_coverage)
   363	
   364	    def get_coverage_count(self) -> int:
   365	        return len(self.global_coverage)
   366	
   367	    def get_coverage_percentage(self, total_edges: int) -> float:
   368	        if total_edges == 0:
   369	            return 0.0
   370	        return len(self.global_coverage) / total_edges * 100.0
   371	
   372	    def map_density(self) -> float:
   373	        """Fraction of the 64KB map that is in use (AFL's map density stat)."""
   374	        return len(self.global_coverage) / self.map_size * 100.0

   383	
   384	    def __init__(self, extras: Optional[Sequence[bytes]] = None):
   385	        self.extras: List[bytes] = sorted(set(extras or []), key=lambda t: (len(t), t))
   386	        self.auto_extras: List[bytes] = []
   387	        self.auto_hits: Dict[bytes, int] = {}

   389	    def maybe_add_auto(self, token: bytes) -> bool:
   390	        """AFL's maybe_add_auto(): remember a token found during bit flipping."""
   391	        if not (MIN_AUTO_EXTRA <= len(token) <= MAX_AUTO_EXTRA):
   392	            return False
   393	        if len(set(token)) <= 1:  # all-same bytes carry no information
   394	            return False
   395	        if token in self.extras:
   396	            return False
   397	        if token in self.auto_hits:
   398	            self.auto_hits[token] += 1
   399	            return False
   400	        self.auto_hits[token] = 1
   401	        if len(self.auto_extras) < MAX_AUTO_EXTRAS:
   402	            self.auto_extras.append(token)
   403	            self.auto_extras.sort(key=lambda t: (len(t), t))
   404	            return True
   405	        # Replace the least useful (largest) entry.
   406	        self.auto_extras[-1] = token
   407	        self.auto_extras.sort(key=lambda t: (len(t), t))
   408	        return True

   411	    def all_tokens(self) -> List[bytes]:
   412	        return list(self.extras) + list(self.auto_extras)

   415	        return len(self.extras) + len(self.auto_extras)

   611	    def save_if_interesting(

   614	        edges: Set[int],

   616	        exec_time: float,
   617	        parent: Optional[TestCase] = None,

   622	        against the *crash* bitmap (``virgin_crash``) and, when its bucketed
   623	        coverage hash is new, filed as a unique crash.  Only inputs that finish
   624	        normally can extend ``virgin_bits`` and become queue entries.
   625	        """

   627	        is_new = False
   628	
   629	        if is_crash:

   631	            if self.crash_bitmap.has_new_bits(trace) > 0:

   640	                    depth=(parent.depth + 1) if parent else 0,
   641	                    creation_time=self.total_execs,

611	    def save_if_interesting(
612	        self,
613	        data: bytes,
614	        edges: Set[int],

616	        exec_time: float,
617	        parent: Optional[TestCase] = None,

620	
621	        Like afl-fuzz.c, a crashing input never enters the queue: it is checked
622	        against the *crash* bitmap (``virgin_crash``) and, when its bucketed
623	        coverage hash is new, filed as a unique crash.  Only inputs that finish
624	        normally can extend ``virgin_bits`` and become queue entries.
625	        """
626	        trace = {e: 1 for e in edges}
627	        is_new = False
628	
629	        if is_crash:
630	            self.total_crash_execs += 1
631	            if self.crash_bitmap.has_new_bits(trace) > 0:
632	                self.crash_bitmap.update(trace)
633	            chash = coverage_hash(edges)
634	            if chash not in self.unique_crash_hashes:
635	                crash_tc = TestCase(
636	                    data=data,
637	                    coverage=set(edges),
638	                    exec_time=exec_time,
639	                    is_crash=True,
640	                    depth=(parent.depth + 1) if parent else 0,
641	                    creation_time=self.total_execs,
642	                )

644	                self.crashes.append(crash_tc)
645	                if self.first_unique_crash_exec is None:
646	                    self.first_unique_crash_exec = self.total_execs
647	            self._record_history()
648	            return False
649	
650	        new_level = self.bitmap.has_new_bits(trace)
651	        if new_level > 0:
652	            self.bitmap.update(trace)
653	            tc = TestCase(
654	                data=data,
655	                coverage=set(edges),
656	                exec_time=exec_time,

677	    def calibrate_case(self, tc: TestCase, cycles: int = CAL_CYCLES) -> float:
678	        """Run a fresh entry several times: stability detection + timing.
679	
680	        Stability is the Jaccard similarity of the coverage observed across
681	        runs; anything below 100% means the target has non-deterministic edges
682	        (AFL calls those "variable" and marks the entry).
683	        """
684	        traces: List[Set[int]] = []
685	        total_time = 0.0
686	        for _ in range(max(1, cycles)):
687	            if self.out_of_budget():
688	                break
689	            edges, _crash, exec_time = self.run_target(tc.data)
690	            traces.append(set(edges))
691	            total_time += exec_time
692	        if not traces:
693	            return 100.0
694	
695	        union: Set[int] = set()
696	        intersection: Optional[Set[int]] = None
697	        for t in traces:
698	            union |= t
699	            intersection = set(t) if intersection is None else (intersection & t)
700	        intersection = intersection or set()
701	        stability = 100.0 if not union else len(intersection) / len(union) * 100.0
702	
703	        tc.exec_time = total_time / len(traces)
704	        tc.coverage = set(union)
705	        tc.is_variable = stability < 100.0  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
706	        tc.stability = stability            # type: ignore[attr-defined]
707	        self.stability_samples.append(stability)
708	        return stability

710	    def trim_case(self, tc: TestCase) -> int:
711	        """Powers-of-two block removal that preserves the entry's coverage."""
712	        if len(tc.data) < TRIM_MIN_BYTES:
713	            return 0
714	
715	        original_len = len(tc.data)
716	        reference = set(tc.coverage)
717	        data = bytearray(tc.data)
718	
719	        len_p2 = 1 << max(0, (len(data) - 1).bit_length())
720	        remove_len = max(len_p2 // TRIM_START_STEPS, TRIM_MIN_BYTES)
721	
722	        while remove_len >= max(len_p2 // TRIM_END_STEPS, 1) and remove_len > 0:
723	            pos = 0
724	            while pos + remove_len <= len(data):
725	                if self.out_of_budget():
726	                    break
727	                candidate = bytes(data[:pos]) + bytes(data[pos + remove_len:])
728	                if not candidate:
729	                    pos += remove_len
730	                    continue
731	                edges, _crash, exec_time = self.run_target(candidate)
732	                if set(edges) == reference:
733	                    data = bytearray(candidate)
734	                    tc.exec_time = exec_time
735	                    # Do not advance: retry the same offset on the shorter buffer.
736	                else:
737	                    pos += remove_len
738	            if self.out_of_budget():
739	                break
740	            remove_len //= 2
741	
742	        removed = original_len - len(data)
743	        if removed > 0:
744	            tc.data = bytes(data)
745	            self.trimmed_bytes += removed
746	        return removed

761	    def cull_queue(self) -> List[TestCase]:
762	        """Greedy set cover over the queue: mark a minimal favoured subset.
763	
764	        Walks the edges in id order, always picking the cheapest entry that
765	        covers a still-uncovered edge (AFL's cull_queue()).
766	        """
767	        for tc in self.queue:
768	            tc.is_favored = False
769	            tc.unique_edges = set()
770	
771	        temp_v: Set[int] = set(self.bitmap.global_coverage)
772	        favored: List[TestCase] = []
773	        for edge in sorted(self.bitmap.global_coverage):
774	            if edge not in temp_v:
775	                continue
776	            best = self.top_rated.get(edge)
777	            if best is None:
778	                candidates = [tc for tc in self.queue if edge in tc.coverage]
779	                if not candidates:
780	                    continue
781	                best = min(candidates, key=lambda t: (self.fav_factor(t), t.creation_time))
782	            newly = temp_v & best.coverage
783	            temp_v -= best.coverage
784	            if not best.is_favored:
785	                best.is_favored = True
786	                best.unique_edges = set(newly)
787	                favored.append(best)
788	            else:
789	                best.unique_edges |= newly
790	
791	        self.pending_favored = sum(1 for tc in self.queue if tc.is_favored and not tc.was_fuzzed)
792	        self.pending_not_fuzzed = sum(1 for tc in self.queue if not tc.was_fuzzed)
793	        return favored

917	    def stage_bitflip1(self, tc: TestCase) -> None:
918	        """Walking 1 bit flips, with auto-dictionary token extraction."""
919	        self._set_stage("bitflip 1/1")
920	        data = bytearray(tc.data)

922	        base_hash = coverage_hash(tc.coverage)
923	        prev_hash = base_hash
924	        collected = bytearray()

926	        for bit in range(nbits):

928	                return
929	            byte_idx, bit_idx = bit // 8, bit % 8
930	            data[byte_idx] ^= 1 << (7 - bit_idx)

937	            # consecutive bytes whose flips all perturb coverage identically

941	                if bit == nbits - 1 and cur_hash == prev_hash:

944	                elif cur_hash != prev_hash:

946	                    prev_hash = cur_hash

948	                    if len(collected) < MAX_AUTO_EXTRA:

"""Core AFL (American Fuzzy Lop) coverage-guided greybox fuzzer.

This module is a faithful, deterministic simulation of afl-fuzz.c's algorithm:

* 64KB shared-memory edge bitmap with hit-count bucketing
  (1, 2, 3, 4-7, 8-15, 16-31, 32-127, 128+),
* edge identification via ``(prev_block >> 1) ^ cur_block`` (AFL's
  ``prev_loc``/``cur_loc`` trick, usually written ``(prev ^ cur) >> 1``),
* a fork-server model that amortises target start-up cost,
* test-case calibration with multi-run stability detection,
* input trimming with powers-of-two block removal preserving coverage,
* corpus culling via greedy set cover (smallest + fastest entry per edge),
* the complete deterministic stage pipeline (walking bit flips 1/2/4, byte
  flips 8/16/32, arithmetics +/- 1..35 for 8/16/32 bit widths in both
  endiannesses, interesting values 8/16/32, auto-dictionary extraction during
  the bit-flip stage and user/auto dictionary insertion),
* the havoc stage (2^1..2^7 stacked random mutations),
* the splice stage (midpoint recombination of two queue entries + havoc),
* performance scoring from execution speed / bitmap size / depth / handicap,
* crash de-duplication through coverage hashing,
* and queue scheduling with favoured-seed priority (the 75/25 skip split).

Everything is driven from a single ``numpy.random.RandomState`` so that a given
seed always produces the same run.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Callable, Dict, Iterable, List, Optional, Sequence, Set, Tuple

import numpy as np

from fuzzsim.bitmap import MAP_SIZE
from fuzzsim.mutation import (
    INTERESTING_8,
    INTERESTING_16,
    INTERESTING_32,
    clone_bytes,
    delete_bytes,
    insert_bytes,
)
from fuzzsim.seed import TestCase

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# AFL tuning constants (config.h)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

ARITH_MAX = 35            # maximum offset used by the arithmetic stages
HAVOC_STACK_POW2 = 7      # havoc stacks 2^1 .. 2^7 mutations
HAVOC_CYCLES = 256        # base havoc iterations (scaled by performance score)
HAVOC_CYCLES_INIT = 1024  # havoc iterations when deterministic stages are off
HAVOC_MIN = 16            # never do fewer than this many havoc execs
HAVOC_MAX_MULT = 16       # performance score cap multiplier (=> max 1600)
HAVOC_BLK_SMALL = 32
HAVOC_BLK_MEDIUM = 128
HAVOC_BLK_LARGE = 1500
SPLICE_CYCLES = 15        # splice attempts per queue entry
SPLICE_HAVOC = 32         # havoc iterations applied to a spliced input

SKIP_TO_NEW_PROB = 75     # favoured/unseen entries: 75/25 split
SKIP_NFAV_OLD_PROB = 95   # skip probability for old non-favoured entries
SKIP_NFAV_NEW_PROB = 75   # skip probability for fresh non-favoured entries

CAL_CYCLES = 3            # calibration executions for a fresh entry
TRIM_MIN_BYTES = 4
TRIM_START_STEPS = 16
TRIM_END_STEPS = 1024

MIN_AUTO_EXTRA = 3
MAX_AUTO_EXTRA = 32
MAX_AUTO_EXTRAS = 50      # auto dictionary capacity
MAX_DET_EXTRAS = 200      # deterministic extras cut-off

# Hit-count buckets used by AFL's classify_counts().
COUNT_CLASS_BUCKETS: Tuple[Tuple[int, int, int], ...] = (
    (0, 0, 0),        # never executed
    (1, 1, 1),        # exactly once
    (2, 2, 2),        # twice
    (3, 3, 4),        # three times
    (4, 7, 8),        # 4-7
    (8, 15, 16),      # 8-15
    (16, 31, 32),     # 16-31
    (32, 127, 64),    # 32-127
    (128, 1 << 30, 128),  # 128+
)


def classify_counts(count: int) -> int:
    """Map a raw hit count onto AFL's 8 hit-count buckets.

    AFL folds hit counts into powers-of-two-ish buckets so that small changes
    in loop trip counts do not look like new coverage::

        1, 2, 3, 4-7, 8-15, 16-31, 32-127, 128+
    """
    if count < 0:
        raise ValueError("hit count must be non-negative")
    for low, high, bucket in COUNT_CLASS_BUCKETS:
        if low <= count <= high:
            return bucket
    return 128


def bucket_index(count: int) -> int:
    """Return the index (0..8) of the bucket a hit count falls into."""
    for idx, (low, high, _bucket) in enumerate(COUNT_CLASS_BUCKETS):
        if low <= count <= high:
            return idx
    return len(COUNT_CLASS_BUCKETS) - 1


def edge_hash(prev_block: int, cur_block: int, map_size: int = MAP_SIZE) -> int:
    """Compute AFL's edge id for the transition ``prev_block -> cur_block``.

    AFL's instrumentation keeps ``prev_loc`` already shifted right by one so
    that A->B and B->A hash differently; the transition is therefore
    ``(prev_block >> 1) ^ cur_block`` taken modulo the bitmap size.
    """
    return ((prev_block >> 1) ^ cur_block) % map_size


def coverage_hash(edges: Iterable[int]) -> str:
    """Stable hash of a coverage set, used for crash de-duplication."""
    payload = ",".join(str(e) for e in sorted(edges)).encode()
    return hashlib.sha1(payload).hexdigest()[:16]


def swap16(value: int) -> int:
    """Byte-swap a 16 bit value."""
    value &= 0xFFFF
    return ((value & 0xFF) << 8) | (value >> 8)


def swap32(value: int) -> int:
    """Byte-swap a 32 bit value."""
    value &= 0xFFFFFFFF
    return (
        ((value & 0x000000FF) << 24)
        | ((value & 0x0000FF00) << 8)
        | ((value & 0x00FF0000) >> 8)
        | ((value & 0xFF000000) >> 24)
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# "Could this value have been produced by a cheaper stage?" predicates
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def could_be_bitflip(xor_val: int) -> bool:
    """True if ``xor_val`` is reachable by the walking bit-flip stages.

    Direct port of afl-fuzz.c's could_be_bitflip(): 1/2/4 bit patterns are
    reachable at any offset, 8/16/32 bit patterns only at byte-aligned ones.
    """
    xor_val &= 0xFFFFFFFF
    if xor_val == 0:
        return True
    sh = 0
    while (xor_val & 1) == 0:
        sh += 1
        xor_val >>= 1
    if xor_val in (1, 3, 15):
        return True
    if sh & 7:
        return False
    return xor_val in (0xFF, 0xFFFF, 0xFFFFFFFF)


def _within_arith(a: int, b: int, bits: int) -> bool:
    """True if ``a`` and ``b`` are within ARITH_MAX using wrapping arithmetic."""
    mask = (1 << bits) - 1
    return ((a - b) & mask) <= ARITH_MAX or ((b - a) & mask) <= ARITH_MAX


def could_be_arith(old_val: int, new_val: int, blen: int) -> bool:
    """True if ``old_val -> new_val`` is reachable by the arithmetic stages."""
    if old_val == new_val:
        return True

    diffs = 0
    ov = nv = 0
    for i in range(blen):
        a = (old_val >> (8 * i)) & 0xFF
        b = (new_val >> (8 * i)) & 0xFF
        if a != b:
            diffs += 1
            ov, nv = a, b

    # A single byte differs: an 8 bit arithmetic op would have found it.
    if diffs == 1 and _within_arith(ov, nv, 8):
        return True

    if blen == 1:
        return False

    # Try 16 bit arithmetics in both endiannesses.
    diffs = 0
    for i in range(blen // 2):
        a = (old_val >> (16 * i)) & 0xFFFF
        b = (new_val >> (16 * i)) & 0xFFFF
        if a != b:
            diffs += 1
            ov, nv = a, b
    if diffs == 1:
        if _within_arith(ov, nv, 16):
            return True
        if _within_arith(swap16(ov), swap16(nv), 16):
            return True

    if blen == 4:
        if _within_arith(old_val, new_val, 32):
            return True
        if _within_arith(swap32(old_val), swap32(new_val), 32):
            return True
    return False


def could_be_interest(old_val: int, new_val: int, blen: int, check_le: bool) -> bool:
    """True if ``old_val -> new_val`` is reachable by the interesting-value stages."""
    if old_val == new_val:
        return True

    # Single-byte interesting values applied at any offset.
    for i in range(blen):
        for interesting in INTERESTING_8:
            tval = (old_val & ~(0xFF << (8 * i))) | ((interesting & 0xFF) << (8 * i))
            if new_val == tval:
                return True

    if blen == 2 and not check_le:
        return False

    for i in range(blen - 1):
        for interesting in INTERESTING_16:
            iv = interesting & 0xFFFF
            tval = (old_val & ~(0xFFFF << (8 * i))) | (iv << (8 * i))
            if new_val == tval:
                return True
            if blen > 2:
                tval = (old_val & ~(0xFFFF << (8 * i))) | (swap16(iv) << (8 * i))
                if new_val == tval:
                    return True
    return False


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Fork server simulation
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class ForkServer:
    """Simulated AFL fork server.

    The real fork server executes the target up to ``main()`` once and then
    clones the initialised process for every test case, which removes the
    (expensive) linking/initialisation cost from the per-exec budget.  We model
    that: ``STARTUP_COST`` is paid once at ``start()`` and every subsequent run
    only pays ``FORK_COST`` plus the target's own execution time.
    """

    STARTUP_COST = 0.020  # 20ms one-off initialisation
    FORK_COST = 0.0002    # 0.2ms per fork
    EXECVE_COST = 0.010   # 10ms if we had to execve() every time

    def __init__(self, program):
        self.program = program
        self.is_running = False
        self.total_execs = 0
        self.total_time = 0.0
        self.startup_time = 0.0
        self.timeouts = 0
        self.child_pid = 0

    def start(self) -> None:
        """Spin up the fork server (paid once)."""
        if self.is_running:
            return
        self.is_running = True
        self.startup_time = self.STARTUP_COST
        self.total_time += self.STARTUP_COST
        self.child_pid = 1000

    def run(self, data: bytes) -> Tuple[Set[int], bool, float]:
        """Execute one test case through the fork server."""
        if not self.is_running:
            self.start()
        self.child_pid += 1
        edges, is_crash, exec_time = self.program.execute(data)
        self.total_execs += 1
        self.total_time += self.FORK_COST + exec_time
        return set(edges), bool(is_crash), float(exec_time)

    def stop(self) -> None:
        self.is_running = False
        self.child_pid = 0

    @property
    def saved_time(self) -> float:
        """Time saved compared to a plain execve() based executor."""
        return self.total_execs * (self.EXECVE_COST - self.FORK_COST) - self.STARTUP_COST


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Bitmap with hit-count bucketing
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class AFLBitmap:
    """64KB coverage bitmap with hit-count bucketing and virgin-bit tracking."""

    def __init__(self, map_size: int = MAP_SIZE):
        self.map_size = map_size
        # virgin_bits[edge] is the OR of every bucket value observed so far.
        self.virgin_bits: Dict[int, int] = {}
        self.global_coverage: Set[int] = set()
        self.hit_counts: Dict[int, int] = {}
        self.trace_bits: Dict[int, int] = {}

    # -- current run ------------------------------------------------------
    def reset_trace(self) -> None:
        self.trace_bits = {}

    def record_trace(self, edges: Dict[int, int]) -> None:
        """Store the raw hit counts of the current execution."""
        self.trace_bits = dict(edges)

    def classified_trace(self) -> Dict[int, int]:
        """Return the current trace after classify_counts()."""
        return {e: classify_counts(c) for e, c in self.trace_bits.items()}

    # -- global bitmap ----------------------------------------------------
    def has_new_bits(self, edges: Dict[int, int]) -> int:
        """AFL's has_new_bits(): 2 = new edge, 1 = new hit-count bucket, 0 = nothing."""
        result = 0
        for edge, count in edges.items():
            if count <= 0:
                continue
            bucket = classify_counts(count)
            seen = self.virgin_bits.get(edge, 0)
            if seen == 0:
                return 2
            if seen & bucket == 0:
                result = max(result, 1)
        return result

    def update(self, edges: Dict[int, int]) -> Set[int]:
        """Fold an execution into the global bitmap, returning new edges."""
        new_edges = set()
        for edge, count in edges.items():
            if count <= 0:
                continue
            if edge not in self.virgin_bits:
                new_edges.add(edge)
                self.virgin_bits[edge] = 0
            self.virgin_bits[edge] |= classify_counts(count)
            self.global_coverage.add(edge)
            self.hit_counts[edge] = self.hit_counts.get(edge, 0) + count
        return new_edges

    def count_bytes(self) -> int:
        """Number of non-zero bytes in the bitmap (AFL's count_bytes)."""
        return len(self.global_coverage)

    def get_coverage_count(self) -> int:
        return len(self.global_coverage)

    def get_coverage_percentage(self, total_edges: int) -> float:
        if total_edges == 0:
            return 0.0
        return len(self.global_coverage) / total_edges * 100.0

    def map_density(self) -> float:
        """Fraction of the 64KB map that is in use (AFL's map density stat)."""
        return len(self.global_coverage) / self.map_size * 100.0


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Dictionary (user supplied extras + auto-extracted tokens)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class Dictionary:
    """User (``-x``) and auto-extracted dictionary tokens."""

    def __init__(self, extras: Optional[Sequence[bytes]] = None):
        self.extras: List[bytes] = sorted(set(extras or []), key=lambda t: (len(t), t))
        self.auto_extras: List[bytes] = []
        self.auto_hits: Dict[bytes, int] = {}

    def maybe_add_auto(self, token: bytes) -> bool:
        """AFL's maybe_add_auto(): remember a token found during bit flipping."""
        if not (MIN_AUTO_EXTRA <= len(token) <= MAX_AUTO_EXTRA):
            return False
        if len(set(token)) <= 1:  # all-same bytes carry no information
            return False
        if token in self.extras:
            return False
        if token in self.auto_hits:
            self.auto_hits[token] += 1
            return False
        self.auto_hits[token] = 1
        if len(self.auto_extras) < MAX_AUTO_EXTRAS:
            self.auto_extras.append(token)
            self.auto_extras.sort(key=lambda t: (len(t), t))
            return True
        # Replace the least useful (largest) entry.
        self.auto_extras[-1] = token
        self.auto_extras.sort(key=lambda t: (len(t), t))
        return True

    @property
    def all_tokens(self) -> List[bytes]:
        return list(self.extras) + list(self.auto_extras)

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        return len(self.extras) + len(self.auto_extras)
